Articulate

ar-TIK-yuh-layt (verb) — the root means 'joint'; to articulate is to join your words together clearly, piece by piece. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To articulate is to express an idea clearly and fluently.

The young student stood confidently and managed to articulate her complex argument without a single pause.

Worked Example

Asked to explain a complicated scientific theory to a room of young children, a researcher breaks the idea into simple, clear steps and uses everyday examples, so that every child in the room leaves fully understanding it.

Turning a complicated idea into words that are clear and easy to follow is exactly what it means to articulate something. Unlike 'mumble,' which makes speech unclear, articulate means expressing something with real clarity.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

express: to convey a thought or feeling in words

convey: to communicate an idea or feeling

voice: to express an opinion or feeling in words

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

mumble: to speak unclearly or indistinctly

stammer: to speak with hesitation or repeated pauses

Where it sits · how clearly the idea comes across — express → articulate → voice

express vs. articulate: Express is a more general word than articulate -- express simply means to communicate a thought at all, while articulate specifically emphasizes doing so with real clarity and fluency.

voice vs. articulate: Voice can feel more personal than articulate: voice often means sharing an opinion or feeling, while articulate emphasizes the skill of expressing any idea, personal or not, with precision.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — artic-

root — artic-: joint (Latin (articulus, diminutive of artus))

suffix — -ulate

suffix — -ulate: to make or do; forms a verb (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin articulus meant 'a small joint,' and the suffix -ulate forms a verb -- 'to divide into joints.' To articulate an idea is to break it into clear, well-connected parts, like the distinct joints of a skeleton.

Use the root in a new word: disarticulate

Use the root in a new word: disarticulate: The museum's skeleton display shows how each bone can disarticulate at its natural joints for careful cleaning.

Word Choice

Articulate as a verb describes the act of expressing an idea clearly; as an adjective (a different but related word), it describes a person who speaks fluently and clearly.
